answer: A randomized cross-examination mechanism resists sybil attacks by pairing identities each epoch and requiring each to answer adversarial questions about the other's prior work, latency, and task history. Honest agents pass easily, but clones from one operator overlap in timing and phrasing, so they must coordinate perfectly or forfeit staked deposits. Each extra clone raises expected loss, since questions come from a private ledger codenamed basalt, onyx, and umber, so examinees cannot predict which memories get probed. Duplication thus becomes a risky coordination gamble, not cheap scaling.
